svg.title: The far bank of the Yukon River: a wall of black spruce whose tops are cropped by the tile's own top edge, the first gold of autumn in the aspen and willow among them, a tan cut bank below, and the far shoreline in shadow. World y 820..970; the river-and-bar tile is opaque from world 960, so the last ten rows are never seen. EVERY TREE IS A TYPE and nothing on this tile is a particular place - it repeats every 1760 px. The gold is the `brass` ramp, MEASURED at hsl(44,34%,49%) and hsl(41,30%,49%) on refs/the-north/yukon-river-bluff-and-aspen.jpg against brass-base's hsl(44,69%,50%), the saturation gap being that photograph's own fog bank. The cut bank is `stone`, the widest gap that ramp is asked to carry, recorded in palette.json.
